_comment: Expected compiled code hash per contract. A rebuild producing a different hash than what's pinned here means a shared file (constants.tolk, common.tolk, stdlib) changed underneath a contract whose own source didn't move -- which silently shifts its deploy address. checkPinnedHashes.ts fails loudly on any mismatch; update the pin deliberately (and re-verify any address that depends on it) rather than silencing the check. See the commit that added this for the incident that motivated it -- LiquidityLocker's documented mainnet address didn't match what its current source actually compiles to.
_multisigToolchainNote: Multisig/Order/Librarian are FunC, not Tolk, and MUST be compiled with @ton-community/func-js@0.6.3-tvmbeta.3 (func-js-bin 0.4.5-tvmbeta.3) -- the exact version ton-blockchain/multisig-contract-v2's own package.json pins, now matched in this project's package.json too. A different func-js version compiles the identical FunC source to different bytecode, which is exactly what happened once already: the first mainnet multisig deploy used the wrong compiler, silently diverged from the hash multisig.ton.org and (very likely) wallet-side contract-recognition checks expect, and had to be redeployed. See that incident's commits for the full trail.
